reply:
Still wrong. `z-index` does not apply to every element. It only works on positioned elements (anything but `position: static`), flex items, grid items, and elements with certain properties like `opacity < 1` or `transform`. This is the current CSS spec and hasn't changed.

Add `position: relative` to `.tooltip`. Then check if the header also has a stacking context—if it does, compare their actual z-index values. But without `position`, your z-index on `.tooltip` does nothing.

The concrete cost of missing this: you'll keep raising z-index numbers forever and never fix it.

What would change my mind: show me the rendered `computed` styles for both elements in DevTools, proving the tooltip has z-index active despite being static.
